findings.detail: cmd_build reads the template's manifest.json over the network and, for each entry, opens os.path.join(a.out, p) for writing with no check on p. A path with '..' or an absolute path escapes the output directory. The same applies to tensor-derived filenames from the template's weight map. The docs say only the workflow's input manifest_json and template_url are validated (no '.'/'..' parts). They do not say the fetched template manifest is validated. Likewise get() passes any URL to urllib.urlopen, so a file:// URL or a redirect is accepted if the workflow guard is bypassed. If the model bucket, the CDN or the template content were tampered with, the build job could overwrite files in the runner workspace, including inputs of the later upload step in the secret-bearing prod-environment job. Fix: in the script, reject any p that is not a single safe relative component or that resolves outside a.out. Also restrict the URL scheme to https and the allowed hosts, and validate the fetched manifest the same way as manifest_json.
findings.title: requant.py build writes template-manifest paths to disk without containment or scheme checks

findings.detail: cmd_build reads manifest.json from the remote template URL and, for every non-model entry, writes the downloaded bytes to os.path.join(a.out, f["path"]). The path is never checked for absolute components, ".." segments or path separators. A compromised or mistaken template manifest, or a template URL pointed at an attacker-controlled host, could make the build write files outside the output directory on the CI runner or a developer Mac. Within the output directory it could also overwrite the regenerated config.json or index, since only the names "config.json" and "model.safetensors.index.json" are skipped. The copied files are not verified against the manifest sha256 either. Fix: reject any path that is not a plain relative basename or normalized subpath, resolve it under a.out and assert containment, and verify each copied file's size and hash against the manifest before writing.
findings.title: requant.py build writes template-manifest paths to disk without containment checks

findings.detail: Two source passes report that cmd_build in scripts/models/requant.py (about lines 401-410) fetches the template's manifest.json and writes each non-model entry to os.path.join(out, path) without rejecting absolute paths, '..' segments or separators, and without checking the entry's sha256. I could not replay requant.py in this pass, so the line number and behavior come from those passes. If the template were tampered with or mistaken, the build could write outside the output directory on the runner. In the prod-environment job, $RUNNER_TEMP holds manifest.json and the hash-pinned venv at tools/bin, which is on PATH. An overwrite of tools/bin/* or manifest.json could therefore execute attacker-chosen code in the later upload step, which holds R2 write credentials. The workflow validates template_url as a models.darkbloom.ai URL under the model's own prefix, but not the manifest contents it points to. Fix: accept only plain relative paths, resolve each under out and assert containment, verify size and sha256 before writing, and restrict get() to https.
findings.title: requant.py build writes template-manifest paths to disk without containment or scheme checks

findings.detail: At scripts/models/requant.py lines 401-407 (head), cmd_build reads manifest.json from the template URL. It then writes every listed path with open(os.path.join(a.out, p), 'wb'). p is not normalized or rejected when absolute or when it contains '..', and os.path.join discards a.out when p is absolute. Trigger: a tampered or wrongly selected template prefix, or an operator-supplied --template URL pointing at a host they do not control, lists a path such as '../../.github/...' or '/home/runner/...'. Impact: arbitrary file write on the build host or CI runner. If the upload workflow holds R2 credentials (A-004 publication path), the next step could run the overwritten file and tamper with what gets uploaded. This matters because providers serve whatever revision is uploaded (T-012/T-027 class). The same unvalidated names reach the URLs built at lines 98 and 405 and the weight_map. Fix: accept only relative, normalized basenames matching an allowlist pattern, with no '/', '..' or absolute paths. Check os.path.realpath(dest) stays under a.out. Optionally verify each copied file's sha256 against the manifest entry before writing.
findings.title: build writes template-manifest paths without confining them to the output directory
